selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does the passage ask you to imagine at the beginning?
questions.answer: A dark time of ignorance and rough living before the light of the Qur’an was seen clearly.

questions.question: What do these bright stars do?
questions.answer: They spread light and push away darkness.

questions.question: What kind of light is especially mentioned?
questions.answer: The light of miraculousness and guidance.

questions.question: What does the earth become like in that picture?
questions.answer: It becomes like a head.

questions.question: How are the stars described after the verses are heard?
questions.answer: As meaningful lights that speak wisdom and truth.

questions.question: What do the stars seem like in that same picture?
questions.answer: They seem like bright, wise, truthful words.

questions.question: What does the passage say each verse scatters?
questions.answer: The darkness of unbelief.

questions.question: What does “a veil of familiarity” mean here in simple words?
questions.answer: Being so used to something that you stop noticing how amazing it is.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person will not truly appreciate if looking too shallowly?
questions.answer: How each verse removed darkness and how beautiful its miraculous recitation is.

questions.question: What big job of the Qur’an is described in this passage?
questions.answer: It lights up darkness and guides people to belief.

questions.question: In the first picture, what kind of age are we asked to imagine?
questions.answer: A time filled with ignorance and roughness.

questions.question: What do they scatter away?
questions.answer: The darkness of unbelief.

questions.question: Before the verses are heard, how do creatures seem to people?
questions.answer: They seem dead or asleep.

questions.question: What do the stars look like to the listeners in this new view?
questions.answer: Like lights that speak truth and show wisdom.

questions.question: What are the land and sea compared to?
questions.answer: To tongues.

questions.question: Why does the passage tell readers to look from that old time instead of only from today?
questions.answer: So they can notice how much light and change the verses brought.

questions.question: What has happened to these verses over time?
questions.answer: Their light has spread and people have come to know them widely.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is sweet about these verses?
questions.answer: Hearing their miraculous beauty.

questions.question: At the start, what are the Qur’an’s verses said to be like?
questions.answer: Bright stars.

questions.question: What kind of darkness is especially mentioned?
questions.answer: The darkness of unbelief.

questions.question: What do the stars become like in the picture given in the passage?
questions.answer: They become like bright words and lights showing wisdom.

questions.question: What happens in the minds of the listeners when they hear the call to glorify Allah?
questions.answer: The world seems to wake up and remember Allah.

questions.question: What does the sky seem like in the picture made by the passage?
questions.answer: It seems like a mouth.

questions.question: Why might a person fail to feel the sweetness and wonder of these verses?
questions.answer: Because the person may be too used to hearing them and look at them only in a shallow way.

title: Reviving Effect of Verses in the Age of Ignorance
